metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets – Jordan

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports descriptive and comparative results from the PISA 2022 assessment administered in 81 countries and economies, including Jordan. The factsheet does not provide the underlying microdata weighting variables (e.g., student sampling weights) or replicate-weight procedures, so the exact weight variable names and whether replicate variance estimation was used are not specified in the provided text. For PISA analyses, analysts typically apply the complex survey design weights supplied with the PISA database to obtain population-representative estimates and correct standard errors under stratification and clustering. Because this document is a results factsheet rather than a re-analysis paper, it should be treated as using OECD’s published PISA estimates; the specific weighting implementation details are therefore not recoverable from the excerpt.

Missing-data handling is not reported because the factsheet does not describe the microdata processing or imputation/deletion rules used to produce the published estimates. This is a reporting/availability limitation of the factsheet format rather than evidence that missing-data handling was not performed in the underlying OECD PISA production process.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample for Jordan consists of 7,799 students in 260 schools who completed the PISA 2022 assessment in mathematics, reading, or science, and for whom creative thinking results are reported in the Jordan factsheet. The excerpt does not specify additional exclusions (e.g., missing background questionnaire items, creative-thinking task completion thresholds, or any imputation rules), so no further filtering criteria beyond the stated completion of the assessment are recoverable from the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet reports Jordan’s performance on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking assessment for 15-year-olds. The creative thinking test contains 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas—across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. In Jordan, students scored a mean of 20 on a 60-point scale, significantly below the OECD average (33), and 36% reached at least Level 3 (baseline proficiency), compared with 78% on average across OECD countries. The factsheet also reports that 34% of the variation in creative thinking within Jordan is uniquely attributed to mathematics performance (correlation 0.66 with mathematics; 0.68 with reading). It further documents within-Jordan gaps by socioeconomic status and gender, and highlights that students’ beliefs and school environment indicators are associated with creative thinking performance in the published PISA results. The document is descriptive and does not provide an ML modeling pipeline, PV estimation procedure, or missing-data strategy for re-analysis.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet rather than an empirical ML study. As such, it does not report an original predictive modeling design, algorithmic training, or target-variable-specific ML performance metrics, so fields like ml_techniques and main_findings are intentionally empty. The factsheet also does not provide microdata-level methodological details (e.g., PV estimation method, missing-data handling, or replicate-weight procedures), because it summarizes OECD’s already-produced PISA estimates.
